title: Falling off your mount
triggers: what happens if i'm knocked off my mount

steps.title: Check what threw you
steps.detail: If the mount is knocked prone, drops to 0 HP, or moves against your will, you have to dismount. You land prone in a space within 5 feet of it.

steps.title: Try to land on your feet
steps.detail: A successful DC 10 Dexterity saving throw lets you dismount safely instead — you land on your feet and skip the fall entirely.

steps.title: Take falling damage, if you actually fell
steps.detail: Being unhorsed at ground level is no drop at all. If the mount was flying or you went off a ledge, it's 1d6 bludgeoning per 10 feet, up to 20d6.

steps.title: You are now prone
steps.detail: Unless you made the save. Standing up costs half your speed, and until you do, melee attackers have advantage on you while ranged attackers have disadvantage.

steps.title: Were you concentrating?
steps.detail: If you took damage and you're holding a concentration spell, make the Constitution save now.

steps.title: What you can still do
steps.detail: Standing costs movement, not your action — you can still attack, cast, or Dash afterwards if you have the movement to spare.

steps.title: Check for instant death first
steps.detail: If the leftover damage after reaching 0 is equal to or greater than your hit point maximum, you die outright — no saves.

steps.title: You fall unconscious and prone
steps.detail: You drop what you're holding, and attacks against you have advantage. Any hit from within 5 feet is an automatic critical.

steps.title: Roll a death save each turn
steps.detail: At the start of each of your turns: 10 or higher is a success, under 10 a failure. Three successes and you stabilise; three failures and you die. Natural 20 wakes you at 1 HP, natural 1 counts as two failures.

steps.title: Damage while down is worse
steps.detail: Any hit that lands on you at 0 HP is an automatic death save failure — two of them if it was a critical.

steps.title: Someone can stabilise you
steps.detail: A DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check or a healer's kit stops the saves. You stay unconscious at 0 HP until you get real healing.

steps.title: Any healing at all brings you back
steps.detail: One point of healing puts you at 1 HP, conscious, with your death saves wiped clean. You're still prone.

title: Keeping concentration after damage
triggers: what dc is my concentration save

steps.title: Work out the DC
steps.detail: It's 10, or half the damage you took — whichever is higher. 26 damage means DC 13; 14 damage still means DC 10.

steps.title: Roll the Constitution save
steps.detail: Add your Constitution modifier, plus proficiency only if you're proficient in Con saves.

steps.title: On a failure the spell ends
steps.detail: It ends immediately, with no action needed from you. Casting it again costs a fresh slot.

steps.title: Watch the other ways it drops
steps.detail: Concentration also ends if you're incapacitated, killed, or cast another concentration spell — the new one replaces the old one.

title: An enemy leaves your reach
prompt: The enemy runs away from me
triggers: do i get a free attack
can i hit them as they leave

steps.title: Did it actually leave your reach?
steps.detail: Moving around inside your reach doesn't trigger anything. It has to leave the area you threaten.

steps.title: Rule out the exceptions
steps.detail: No opportunity attack if it took the Disengage action, teleported, or was moved without spending its own movement — being shoved or thrown doesn't provoke.

steps.title: Spend your reaction
steps.detail: One melee attack, resolved as it leaves. You only have one reaction per round, so using it here means you can't use it again until your next turn.

title: Grabbing hold of someone
triggers: how do i escape a grapple

steps.title: Check you can
steps.detail: You need at least one free hand, and the target can be at most one size larger than you.

steps.title: Swap an attack for the attempt
steps.detail: Grappling replaces one of your attacks, so with Extra Attack you can swing once and grapple with the other.

steps.title: Roll the contest
steps.detail: Your Strength (Athletics) against the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) — their choice. Ties go to the defender.

steps.title: On a win, their speed is 0
steps.detail: They're grappled until you let go, you're incapacitated, or something moves them out of your reach.

steps.title: Escaping later
steps.detail: On their turn they can spend an action to repeat the contest against your Athletics.

steps.title: Compare Stealth to passive Perception
steps.detail: Everyone sneaking rolls Stealth. Anyone whose passive Perception is beaten doesn't notice you — and is surprised.

steps.title: Roll initiative as normal
steps.detail: There is no separate 'surprise round'. Everyone rolls initiative and the order runs as usual.

steps.title: Surprised creatures lose their first turn
steps.detail: No movement, no action, no reaction until their first turn ends — even if they act late in the order.

steps.title: Attacks against them
steps.detail: Attacking a surprised creature isn't automatically advantage — that comes from being unseen, so check whether you're actually hidden from it.

steps.title: Measure the drop
steps.detail: 1d6 bludgeoning for every 10 feet, capped at 20d6 — so anything past 200 feet hurts exactly the same.

steps.title: You land prone
steps.detail: Unless the fall's damage was negated entirely.

steps.title: Check concentration
steps.detail: The damage counts, so any concentration spell needs a Con save at DC 10 or half the damage.

steps.title: Did it drop you to 0?
steps.detail: If the fall took you to 0 hit points, follow the dying rules from there.

title: Why can't I hit this thing?

steps.title: Start with the roll itself
steps.detail: d20 + ability modifier + proficiency, against the target's AC. Meet it or beat it.

steps.title: Is anything giving disadvantage?
steps.detail: Firing a ranged weapon with an enemy within 5 feet, being prone, poisoned, frightened, or restrained all impose it.

steps.title: Is the target behind cover?
steps.detail: Half cover is +2 to its AC, three-quarters is +5, and total cover means you can't target it at all.

steps.title: Can you actually see it?
steps.detail: Attacking what you can't see is disadvantage, and dim light or darkness may be the real culprit.
